definition: The tanh activation — a scaled sigmoid squashing outputs to (−1, 1); once ubiquitous in RNNs, now largely displaced by ReLU-family functions.
details: The tanh activation — a scaled sigmoid squashing outputs to (−1, 1); once ubiquitous in RNNs, now largely displaced by ReLU-family functions.

explainer.lead: Tanh is a scaled sigmoid that squashes outputs into (−1, 1). It was once ubiquitous in RNNs and is now largely displaced by ReLU-family functions.

tiers.eli5: It squeezes any number into the range between minus one and one, so very big or very small inputs stop growing.
tiers.practitioner: Used where bounded, zero-centred activations help, such as recurrent hidden states and gated architectures. Pitfall: it saturates for large inputs, so gradients vanish in deep or long stacks.
tiers.paperLevel: tanh(x) = (e^x − e^−x)/(e^x + e^−x), a scaled sigmoid with output range (−1, 1). Limits: saturating gradients for large magnitudes; superseded in many feedforward networks by ReLU-family functions.

explainer.example: An RNN cell passes its pre-activation through tanh so each hidden value stays between −1 and 1.
